newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler U.S. June vehicle sales fall 4 percent.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler U.S. June vehicle sales fall 4 percent.

text.p: Chrysler Corp. on Tuesday reported a 4 percent decline in its June U.S. light vehicle sales from a year ago, a smaller drop than analysts had expected.
The No. 3 automaker said it sold 219,756 vehicles in the month, compared with 228,828 for June 1996. Chrysler said the figures represent its third best June in company history.
Industry analysts had expected a decline of 10 percent.

Chrysler's passenger car sales fell 14 percent to 72,480 units. Light trucks, including pickup trucks, minivans and sport utility vehicles, rose 2 percent to 147,276. Combined minivan sales, helped by increased incentives ranging from $750 to $1,000, rose 2 percent to their best finish so far this year.

"We had a strong finish for Jeep Cherokee, Grand Cherokee and Dodge Dakota -- strong enough to help us set a June record for light truck sales," James Holden, executive vice president for sales and marketing, said in a statement.
Chrysler was the first major automaker to report June sales. Subaru of America Inc., a unit of Fuji Heavy Industries Ltd., reported a June sales increase of 17 percent to 10,329 units.
General Motors Corp. is scheduled to report its June sales Wednesday, followed by Ford Motor Co. on Thursday.
